findings.reason: The protected implementation is concise, direct, and expert-interview-ready. `previous`, `run_length`, `character`, and `total` expose the maximal-run state and accumulation without auxiliary collections or indirect control flow. The empty-string sentinel is visibly outside the lowercase input alphabet, every branch has a necessary role, and no prohibited generic `index` binding appears. No material improvement warrants a candidate.

After each character, `run_length` equals the length of the maximal equal-character suffix ending at that position: it increments on equality with `previous` and resets to one at a run boundary. Exactly `run_length` qualifying substrings end there, one for every suffix length from one through the current run. Adding that contribution counts every one-distinct-letter substring exactly once by its unique ending position, while no interval crossing a character change can qualify.

An independent brute-force oracle constructed a character set while extending every start position and stopped after a second distinct letter appeared. The oracle, protected app source, immutable native source, and independently written start-and-extend control agreed on all seven authored cases, all three benchmark outputs, 9,840 exhaustive strings over `a`, `b`, and `c` through length eight, and 10,000 deterministic random strings generated with seed 1180. Random coverage included 171 singletons, 735 uniform strings, 3,837 strings with every adjacent pair different, 5,811 returning-character patterns, and broad coverage of both `a` and `z`.

The visible suite exercises the exact minimum length with `s = "z"` and the exact maximum length with a 1,000-character alternating string. A singleton returns one, a uniform run accumulates `1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n + 1) / 2`, every-adjacent-different input contributes one per position, separated copies of the same letter remain different runs, and several run lengths contribute independent triangular counts.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1180, Python, and native entrypoint `Solution.countLetters`. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the required count of substrings with one distinct letter, two examples, two constraints, and three hints. The app-local `solve(s)` signature preserves nonempty lowercase input, contiguous nonempty interval semantics, occurrence rather than distinct-text counting, and the integer return value.

The immutable native source remains bound to verified submission 2067898495 and is unchanged. Apart from the required LeetCode class and method wrapper, protected app and native sources initialize identical scalar state, apply the same equality/reset recurrence for every character, add the same run length, and return the same total. solve.py, leetcode.py, and submission.json were not edited.

The independently correct O(n^2) control passed all 10 outputs but failed only scaling at 171.23x/+1.36. benchmark.json remained byte-for-byte unchanged.
